findings.evidence: Caption: 'A (left): layer-by-layer, Part I → VI, building the substrate then the discipline. B (right): question-by-question: six independent navigation prompts, each mapped to the chapter that answers it.'
findings.issue: The figure's panel B lists six prompts, but the caption calls them 'six independent navigation prompts' while panel B in the rendered image contains only five visible prompt boxes plus a sixth implied; more importantly the caption says 'each mapped to the chapter that answers it' but the figure shows multiple chapters per prompt (e.g. 'fits host? → KV Ch3/7'). The caption overstates the one-to-one mapping it describes.
findings.fix_instruction: Reword the caption to 'each mapped to the chapter(s) that answer it' to match the multi-chapter arrows actually drawn.

findings.evidence: p.29, §2.3: 'An NVIDIA H100 delivers ~989 TFLOPS (BF16 dense tensor-core peak, without sparsity) [1P][FACT], which is 0.989 PFLOPS. (Here and throughout we quote the dense, no-sparsity tensor-core peak for any precision; NVIDIA's datasheet prints the 2× with-sparsity figure — 1,979 TFLOPS for FP16/BF16 — as its headline number, so a dense-vs-sparse note is required even in vendor material.)' The text says 'NVIDIA's datasheet prints the 2× with-sparsity figure — 1,979 TFLOPS for FP16/BF16 — as its headline number'. Checking: 989 × 2 = 1,978, not 1,979. The actual NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet figure is 1,979 TFLOPS (with sparsity). The book correctly states 1,979, and 989 × 2 = 1,978 ≈ 1,979 (the datasheet rounds up). However, the text writes '1,979 TFLOPS' and elsewhere (p.161, Table 8-1) writes '~1,979 TFLOPS with sparsity ÷ 2' — the division 1,979 ÷ 2 = 989.5, which the book presents as '989 TFLOPS'. The half-TFLOP rounding (989.5 → 989) is never acknowledged. This is a rounding of a vendor-published figure, presented as if exact.
findings.issue: Table 8-1 (p.161) derives the dense peak as '1,979 TFLOPS with sparsity ÷ 2' = 989 TFLOPS, but 1,979 ÷ 2 = 989.5. The half-TFLOP is silently truncated to 989. The vendor's dense figure may itself be 989 or 989.5 — the book presents the division as producing exactly 989 without noting the rounding. This is a very minor rounding presentation issue, not an arithmetic error (989.5 ≈ 989), but the derivation '1,979 ÷ 2' implies an exact halving that yields a non-integer.
findings.fix_instruction: In Table 8-1's derivation cell, write '1,979 TFLOPS with sparsity ÷ 2 ≈ 989 TFLOPS (vendor dense figure, rounded)' or simply cite the dense figure directly from the datasheet rather than deriving it by halving the sparse figure.

findings.evidence: Figure 2 (p. 15-16 of PDF) in-figure labels: 'token → cost? Ch4', 'fits host? → KV Ch3/7', 'which phase binds? Ch2/8', '1 host or fleet? Ch17', 'who serves it? Ch10/11/20', 'is it the right call? Ch16/22/25'. Caption: "B (right): question-by-question: six independent navigation prompts, each mapped to the chapter that answers it. These question-to-chapter links are starting points, not complete coverage: one question often spans several chapters, and the decision-justification chapters (Ch. 22 for the design loop, Ch. 25 for the recorded Architecture Decision Record) carry the reasoning the prompt points toward."
findings.issue: Figure-vs-caption and List-of-Figures inconsistency in the figure's own reference syntax. The figure's in-figure pointers use a bare chapter-number form ('Ch4', 'Ch3/7', 'Ch2/8', 'Ch16/22/25') with no § anchors and with inconsistent spacing ('Ch4' vs 'Ch 3/7'), whereas the caption refers to 'Ch. 22' and 'Ch. 25' — the same targets in two different notations. More substantively, the mapping in the figure does not match the Preface's own checklist (p. 14): the figure maps 'fits host? → KV' to 'Ch3/7' and 'which phase binds?' to 'Ch2/8', matching the checklist's Q2/Q3 — but the figure's first prompt, 'token → cost?', is mapped only to 'Ch4', whereas the checklist's Q1 is 'What is the workload?' (Ch 4) and token accounting is spread across Chs 1–3; 'token → cost?' therefore has no chapter that answers it as posed. The caption's claim that each prompt is 'mapped to the chapter that answers it' is thus not true for the first prompt.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-map the figure's first prompt to 'tokens? Ch1' and add 'workload → Ch4' as a separate prompt so the six figure prompts match the Preface's six checklist items one-for-one; normalise the in-figure pointers to the book's 'Ch. N' form (with § anchors where a specific section is meant), and update the caption so 'the chapter that answers it' is true of every prompt.

findings.evidence: Figure 2 in-figure left column labels: 'A · LAYER-BY-LAYER (Parts I → VI)', 'I · The Token', 'II · The Workload', 'III · The System', 'IV · The Architecture', 'V · The Fleet', 'VI · The Architect', 'build the substrate, then the discipline'; right column: 'B · QUESTION-BY-QUESTION', 'each question → the chapter that answers it'.
findings.issue: In-figure heading divergence from the caption and from the List of Figures. The List of Figures (p. 9) records Fig 2 as 'Reading the book two ways'. The caption describes panel A as 'layer-by-layer, Part I → VI, building the substrate then the discipline' — matching the figure — but the figure's own left-panel title is 'A · LAYER-BY-LAYER (Parts I → VI)' while the heading above the columns reads 'layer-by-layer (Parts), or question-by-question (traceability)'. The right-hand title 'B · QUESTION-BY-QUESTION' carries the parenthetical '(traceability)' in the figure's top rule, yet the caption never mentions traceability and the figure's own bottom rule instead says 'each question → the chapter that answers it'. Three different descriptions of panel B's purpose appear in one figure (traceability / question-by-question / chapter mapping), and the caption does not reconcile them. This is the in-figure-title-vs-caption divergence family flagged in the blind-spot note.
findings.fix_instruction: Make panel B's purpose statement singular: if the intent is traceability, title it 'B · QUESTION-BY-QUESTION (traceability)' and drop 'each question → the chapter that answers it'; if the intent is chapter mapping, drop '(traceability)' from the top rule. Ensure the caption states the same purpose and that the List of Figures entry ('Reading the book two ways') is consistent with both.

findings.evidence: p. 16 (Preface §'Read the book two ways'): "B · QUESTION-BY-QUESTION — token → cost? Ch4; fits host? → KV Ch3/7; which phase binds? Ch2/8; 1 host or fleet? Ch17; who serves it? Ch10/11/20; is it the right call? Ch16/22/25" — against the Contents (p. 7-8), where Ch 4 is 'The Anatomy of an AI Workload' and Ch 17 is 'From Server to Fleet'.
findings.issue: Ambiguous referent / reuse of a quantity with two meanings in the same figure panel: 'token → cost?' maps only to Ch 4 ('The Anatomy of an AI Workload'), but the cost of a token is derived in Ch 16 ('TCO: The Total Cost Reality Check') and the token unit itself is Ch 1 ('It All Starts With the First Token'). As written the prompt names a quantity ('token cost') whose chapter is Ch 1 + Ch 16 but is pointed at Ch 4, so the prompt and its target disagree. The same pattern appears in the other five prompts, whose target chapters (Chs 3/7, 2/8, 17, 10/11/20, 16/22/25) match the Preface checklist's chapter sets, so the first prompt is the outlier. Note also that the figure's '1 host or fleet? Ch17' target is Ch 17 only, whereas the checklist's Q4 is answered by Chs 16–17.
findings.fix_instruction: Align Figure 2's right panel one-for-one with the six checklist items on p. 14 (Q1 workload → Ch 4; Q2 fits one host → Chs 3, 7; Q3 which phase binds → Chs 2, 8; Q4 how many hosts → Chs 16–17; Q5 who serves it → Chs 10–11, 20; Q6 is it the right call → Chs 16, 22, 25) and update the prompt wording so each names the quantity its targets actually answer.
